page: UpCloud PREMIUM-48xCPU-96GB is a KVM-based virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor. It features 48 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. Local storage consists of a bundled 400 GB SSD, and the network configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results place this server's processing capabilities in the top tier. The AMD EPYC CPU achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 3910.08 and a multi-core score of 140457.32, both ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. This raw compute power is complemented by strong memory bandwidth, measuring 261.26 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 109.87 GB/sec for writes. Single-threaded gzip compression reaches 43.07 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scales to 640.54 GB/sec, reflecting highly efficient parallel execution.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is optimized for compute-dense workloads rather than memory-intensive applications. While its PassMark CPU score of 84358.21 is in the top 10%, its PassMark memory score of 2231.38 falls in the middle 50%, highlighting a potential bottleneck for memory-bound tasks. The server is highly effective for high-throughput static web serving, database operations, and CPU-based machine learning tasks, such as small-model LLM prompt processing which achieves 4575.29 tokens/sec. It is well-suited for parallel processing, CI/CD pipelines, and compute-heavy microservices.

It includes a bundled 400 GB local SSD and one public IPv4 address. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier processing capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 140457.32 and a PassMark CPU score of 84358.21, both placing in the top 10%. Memory performance is solid, with large-block read bandwidth reaching 261.26 GB/sec, though its PassMark memory score remains in the average tier. This resource profile makes the instance highly efficient for parallelized, compute-heavy workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and lightweight LLM prompt processing, while presenting a tradeoff for applications requiring massive memory footprints.
